title: Orion ScaleWorks AI — Enterprise Evaluation Notes (Customer Success)
account_snapshot: Company: Orion ScaleWorks AI (orionscaleworks.ai). Original HubSpot stage was evaluation; as of 2026-03-21 they are in late-stage technical validation pending legal + procurement paperwork.
products_in_scope: Dedicated + Private + Optimize (same as initial eval). Primary buyer motion is dedicated capacity with explicit SLA metrics.
use_cases_in_scope: Chat assistant, transactional risk scoring, embeddings search, reranking (no scope expansion since early Feb).
deployment_requirements_update: Update vs earlier notes: they no longer require on-prem for the pilot. Current requirement is VPC deployment with private connectivity; they want an option to serve an EU subset in-region (data residency) later in rollout.
security_requirements_summary: SSO/SAML, SOC2, ISO27001, audit logging, customer-managed keys via KMS, data residency controls for EU subset, retention controls. Update: audit log retention requirement is now 'minimum 24 months' (was previously discussed as >= 12 months).
commercials_update: Estimated annualized spend is trending above initial band due to increased reserved capacity ask; internal working range: 500k–1.0M ARR depending on reserved GPU count + EU footprint. Forecast close moved from 2026-05 to 2026-06 due to legal review and procurement cycle length.
key_contacts_customer: CTO is driving tail-latency requirements and will not approve without a stable 99th percentile story. Infra team owns load testing + VPC connectivity. Legal is focused on data residency language + uptime credits.
competitors_mentioned: OpenAI, Anthropic, AWS Bedrock, Azure OpenAI (Azure came up in 2026-03-18 runbook review as a fallback for EU routing).
current_blockers: 1) Data residency clause: need clearer definition of what constitutes 'processing' vs 'storage' for prompts + logs. 2) Reserved GPU procurement: finance now aligned in principle, but requires final quote + ramp schedule. 3) Tail latency: long-tail prompts improved but they want one more 72h soak with the updated kernel/config to sign off.
what_changed_since_2026_03_12: Tail latency issue is no longer at '2% long-tail prompts' as previously observed; after kernel/config changes, remaining spikes are rarer and correlate with a specific prompt class (SQL-like strings + long tool output). On-prem requirement de-scoped for pilot. Close date slipped to June due to legal/procurement.
next_steps: Finalize the revised soak-test spec (72h) + capture acceptance criteria in the SLA appendix draft. Schedule infra handoff for VPC peering runbook. Legal: provide updated redline responses on data residency + uptime credits; align on log retention language (24 months) and what is customer-configurable.
timeline: 2026-01-20: Initial intro (AE) — high-level requirements: latency SLOs, 99th pct targets, reserved capacity.
2026-01-27: Infra questionnaire sent (SE) — requested traffic profiles, token distribution, peak QPS.
2026-02-12: Deep dive with infra — discussed kernel selection + quantization tolerance.
2026-02-18: POC kickoff — agreed on load test harness + representative prompt set + soak window.
2026-02-25: Perf bench (phase 1) — microbench on small scale, throughput ceiling per GPU documented.
2026-03-02: Soak test (phase 2) — 24h run; memory pressure at ~10k concurrent KV-cache sessions; bug filed for KV-cache persistence edge case.
2026-03-08: Security review — shared SOC2 materials; discussed KMS integration and audit log retention expectations.
2026-03-12: SLA negotiation — legal submitted redlines on data residency + uptime credits.

2026-03-18: Tech runbook review — walked through VPC peering + observability; customer asked to remove on-prem requirement for pilot and focus on VPC-only. Azure OpenAI mentioned as EU contingency option.
2026-03-20: Perf follow-up — reviewed updated kernel/config results; agreed to rerun soak for 72h with expanded prompt set including SQL-like edge cases.
detailed_notes: POC focus remains dedicated capacity performance + guaranteed throughput for transactional scoring. They keep repeating: stable tail latency matters more than small median improvements.
Traffic profile (unchanged): bursty QPS around release windows; baseline ~1.2k QPS embeddings, ~300 QPS chat assistant; peak planning target ~5k QPS with autoscale/burst behavior.
Latency/SLO targets (still the anchor): 95th pctl < 70ms and 99th pctl < 150ms for short-chat flows (<=512 tokens). They want SLOs explicitly tied to SLA language, not 'best effort.'

Reserved GPU ask (updated): initial commit is still framed as 8x H100-equivalent reserved, but they now want a written ramp plan that can reach 32x within the next two quarters if pilot KPIs are met (previously discussed as scaling to ~24x).

Benchmark plan (same structure, updated soak): phase 1 microbench (kernels + quant profiles), phase 2 scaled load tests (synthetic QPS matching token distro), phase 3 soak. Update: phase 3 soak is now 72h instead of 24h, and must include the problematic prompt class (SQL-like strings) as a dedicated slice of the run.

Representative prompts (unchanged categories): transactional fraud-check prompts, multi-turn chat (~6 turns avg), dense embeddings (2–4k char blobs), reranking sets (top-100 candidates). Update: add a 'SQL-like + tool-output' bucket with strict reporting on p99/p99.9.

Observed issues: latency spikes are now less frequent and more diagnosable; remaining concern is occasional long-tail stalls under mixed workload. Customer wants an explicit mitigation/guardrail (prompt classification + routing, or a config that caps worst-case).

Security notes: require SSO/SAML + org-owned KMS for keys. Audit log retention requirement clarified to 24 months minimum. Data residency: EU subset must be served in-region; they also want clarity on where telemetry/logs are stored and for how long.
Quote (CTO, repeated): 'We can tolerate a small median shift but not 99th percentile regressions.' (Still the north star.)

CS risk: if legal drags past April, they may split the deal into (a) US-only pilot on dedicated and (b) separate EU addendum later. They asked if pricing changes between phases; we should keep terms stable if possible.
Internal note: emphasize our ability to provide audit logs + retention controls as customer-configurable settings; legal will ask whether retention is default vs configurable.
